# The gap: rectangles {#sec-rectangles}

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/book.R")
```

There are three ways through R's subsetting code, and an ALTREP array is
treated differently on each.

| You write | R calls | The array sees | Can it plan? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x[i]` | `VectorSubset()` | `Extract_subset`, every index at once | yes |
| `x[cbind(i, j, k)]` | `VectorSubset()` after `mat2indsub()` | `Extract_subset`, every index at once | yes |
| `x[i, j, k]`, `m[i, j]` | `ArraySubset()`, `MatrixSubset()` | `Elt`, one element at a time | no |

In the third row R has done the hard part already. `ArraySubset()` and
`MatrixSubset()` turn each subscript (negative, logical, character,
missing) into a vector of positive positions, one per dimension. That list
is the hyperslab. R then walks every output cell and asks the object for
that one element.

The patch offers the list to the object first. If the object's class has
an `Extract_array_subset` method and it returns the values, R skips the
walk. Otherwise nothing changes.

## The example

A simulated store, so that the only thing measured is how R asks: 48
million doubles in 480 chunks, never allocated, and a 12 million cell
matrix. Each fetch call takes 50 ms however many chunks it carries, the
way one round of concurrent requests does.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| file: scripts/02-rectangles.R
```

```{r}
res <- book_run("02-rectangles.R")
book_table(res)
```

The chunk counts match across builds: the patch does not change what is
read, only how it is asked for. On stock R the store hears from R once per
chunk, in series, in between a great many single-element calls:

```{r}
book_elt(res)
```

The last row is the workaround that exists today. `altarr_extract()` does
the planned read on any R, and it is the same speed in both builds. But it
is a function you have to know about and call. Code written for arrays
calls `[`.

## Why the element loop cannot be rescued from the inside

A class can make `Elt` fast for a cached chunk, and altarr does. What it
cannot do from inside `Elt` is know what is coming. The first element of
a 250 x 250 x 15 block looks the same as a lone `x[1, 1, 1]`. Guessing
(read ahead on a miss) fetches chunks nobody wanted when the guess is
wrong. R knows the whole request. The method is how it says so.
